Confirmed: AGENTS.md has no `2.2` subsection — section 2 is a flat numbered list. I've verified the design's claims against the actual repo state (catalog rows, merged specs, client code, module coverage tables, and the forbidden-marker lists). The design is largely accurate and well-grounded, but its shared leak-marker helper doesn't actually fix the inconsistency it describes as the problem.

```gaos-review

  - severity: major   scope: ".gaos/packet/design.md"   note: "The shared leak-marker helper (src/utils/server-leak-markers.ts) is introduced to end the disagreement between the data-driven harness's default marker list and the hand-written TC-VSYS-006 spec's own marker list, but the design never updates either of those two existing lists to use it — after the change there are three independent marker lists instead of the two the design calls a problem, so the stated goal of giving a future reader one authoritative set is not met."
  - severity: nit   scope: ".gaos/packet/design.md"   note: "The new response-body leak-check assertion is placed in a new file under src/utils/ instead of next to the repo's existing shared response-assertion helpers (expectJson/expectStatus) in src/api/core/assertions.ts, so assertion helpers for responses now live in two different places with no stated reason for the split."
  - severity: nit   scope: ".gaos/packet/design.md"   note: "The design cites 'AGENTS.md §2.2' for the no-raw-request-in-specs rule, but AGENTS.md's golden-rules section is a flat numbered list with no §2.2 subsection, so the citation does not resolve to anything in the actual file."
```

```gaos-handoff
No blockers found in the design against the BRD/catalog/policy rules; the design's architecture (client methods, spec placement, catalog follow-up) is sound and matches established repo conventions. One major finding: the shared leak-marker helper under-delivers on its own stated purpose of ending a two-list disagreement, since it adds a third list rather than resolving the first two. Two nits on helper placement and an AGENTS.md citation. None of these block the design from proceeding to implementation, but the major finding should be addressed (either by having the implementer unify the lists, or by the architect revising the design) before the five specs are built against it.
```
